sources_considered.why: Reports xAI/SpaceX AI capex for Q1 2026 from the IPO prospectus.
Reuters report of the Meta–Nebius compute purchase deal.
Meta's Q2 2026 capex and full-year guidance.
Primary source showing Meta buying gigawatt-scale AI GPUs, with shipments starting in 2H 2026.
The primary Meta release has the same capex figures, but its text has line breaks that make exact quotation unreliable. A news copy was used instead.
The Meta–Google TPU rental value is unconfirmed. It was not needed.

receipt.public_excerpt: AI capital expenditures reached $7.72 billion in the first quarter of 2026, up from $2.57 billion a year earlier.

evidence_items.explanation: xAI is neither OpenAI nor Anthropic. Its AI compute spending in a single quarter of 2026 was $7.72 billion, well above 'barely a few billion' a year. This spending came before xAI's May deal to rent capacity to Anthropic.

receipt.public_excerpt: Nebius signed an initial $3 billion deal with Meta in November and a$17.4 billion deal with Microsoft in September.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that, before 2026, compute buyers other than OpenAI and Anthropic were already signing multibillion-dollar neocloud contracts. These deals fall outside the 2026 target period, so this is context only.

receipt.public_excerpt: The deal is the latest example of U.S. ⁠tech giants'efforts to supplement ​their own AI data-centre build-outs by locking in scarce GPU and power capacity from "neocloud" providers like Nebius.

evidence_items.explanation: In March 2026, Meta signed a deal to buy $12 billion of AI compute from Nebius, with up to $15 billion more. This is third-party compute demand from a buyer other than OpenAI and Anthropic, far above a few billion dollars.

metric_scope.metric: AI compute purchase commitment (Nebius contract value)

evidence_items.locator: paragraph beginning 'Capital expenditures, including principal payments'

receipt.public_excerpt: Capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, amounted to $31.08bn.

evidence_items.explanation: Meta spent $31 billion on capex in Q2 2026 alone. The source does not say what share was AI compute, so this is context. Together with AMD's release on Meta's gigawatt-scale AI GPU deployment, it shows Meta's own compute demand is far above a few billion dollars.

metric_scope.metric: Capital expenditures including finance lease principal

receipt.public_excerpt: AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) and Meta today announced a 6-gigawatt agreement to power Meta’s next generation of AI infrastructure across multiple generations of AMD Instinct GPUs.

evidence_items.explanation: Primary confirmation that Meta is buying AI GPUs at gigawatt scale for its own workloads in 2026. The release gives no dollar figure.

unresolved_gaps: There is no official total for 2026 AI compute spending by all buyers other than OpenAI and Anthropic.
Some xAI/SpaceX capacity was later rented to Anthropic, starting May 2026. The Q1 2026 capex came before that deal, but part of the build may now serve Anthropic.
Meta's capex is not broken out between AI compute and other infrastructure.
